knowledge:
- key_parameters: min_score=threshold for matching PWMs, e.g., "70%" ;; best_only=if TRUE, subsets results to only the highest-scoring match per sequence ;; break_ties=controls tie-breaking for identical scores, with options "random", "first", "last", "central", or "all" ;; abs=if TRUE, assesses absolute distance from the sequence center (first bin starts at zero) ;; model=statistical model for enrichment testing, with options "poisson", "quasi", or "iteration" ;; exclude=genomic regions to exclude when generating background ranges (e.g., N-rich regions) ;; n_iter=number of iterations for generating background ranges (e.g., 100, 1000, 5000)
- alternatives: centrimo (from MEME-Suite) is a popular tool for positional bias analysis; testMotifPos() is an R-native alternative that does not assume centrality and uses binomial tests with harmonic mean p-values ;; writeXStringSet (from Biostrings) can be used to export background sequences to a fasta file if performing enrichment testing outside of motifTestR
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing transcription factor binding motifs (TFBMs) in genomic regions of interest (such as ChIP-Seq or ATAC-Seq peaks) within the R/Bioconductor environment, specifically to detect positional localization or overall enrichment compared to a matched background.
- pitfalls: Sequences containing Ns (e.g., centromeres, telomeres) produce warning messages when matching PWMs; use exclude in makeRMRanges to avoid these regions ;; The Poisson model for enrichment can yield anti-conservative p-values if counts are over-dispersed ;; The Iterative model is the slowest and requires a large number of iterations (>1000) for reliable p-values (minimum p-value is 1/n_iterations) ;; Positional bias results are dependent on the pre-determined bin-size, unlike centrimo's adaptive methods.

workflows.name: positional_bias_analysis
workflows.intent: Identify transcription factor binding motifs that show positional bias (localization) relative to the centers of a set of genomic sequences.
workflows.stages: 1. Extract sequences from genomic peaks using getSeq() ;; 2. Find PWM matches in the sequences using getPwmMatches() ;; 3. Test for positional bias using testMotifPos() ;; 4. Visualize the positional distribution of matches using plotMatchPos()
workflows.code:
test_seq <- getSeq(BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19, ar_er_peaks)
names(test_seq) <- as.character(ar_er_peaks)
score_thresh <- "70%"
getPwmMatches(ex_pfm$ESR1, test_seq, min_score = score_thresh)
getPwmMatches(ex_pfm$ESR1, test_seq, min_score = score_thresh, best_only = TRUE)
bm_all <- getPwmMatches(
  ex_pfm, test_seq, min_score = score_thresh, best_only = TRUE, break_ties = "all",
  mc.cores = cores
)
countPwmMatches(ex_pfm, test_seq, min_score = score_thresh, mc.cores = cores)
res_pos <- testMotifPos(bm_all, mc.cores = cores)
res_abs <- testMotifPos(bm_all, abs = TRUE, mc.cores = cores)
topMotifs <- res_pos |>
    subset(fdr < 0.05) |>
    rownames()
A <- plotMatchPos(bm_all[topMotifs], binwidth = 10, se = FALSE)
B <- plotMatchPos(
    bm_all[topMotifs], binwidth = 10, geom = "col", use_totals = TRUE
) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~name)
A + B + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") & theme(legend.position = "bottom")

workflows.name: motif_enrichment_analysis
workflows.intent: Test for overall enrichment of motifs in a set of test sequences compared to a genomic-feature-matched background control set.
input: hg19_mask (GRanges object of masked genomic regions)
workflows.stages: 1. Annotate peaks by genomic features ;; 2. Define background ranges using GRangesList ;; 3. Generate randomly-selected, size-matched background ranges using makeRMRanges() ;; 4. Extract background sequences using getSeq() ;; 5. Test for motif enrichment using testMotifEnrich() with quasi or iteration models
workflows.code:
ar_er_peaks$feature <- ifelse(
  overlapsAny(ar_er_peaks, zr75_enh), "enhancer", "other"
)
chr1 <- GRanges(sq)[1]
bg_ranges <- GRangesList(
  enhancer = zr75_enh,
  other = GenomicRanges::setdiff(chr1, zr75_enh)
)
rm_ranges <- makeRMRanges(
  splitAsList(ar_er_peaks, ar_er_peaks$feature),
  bg_ranges, exclude = hg19_mask,
  n_iter = 100
)
rm_seq <- getSeq(BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19, rm_ranges)
mcols(rm_seq) <- mcols(rm_ranges)
enrich_res <- testMotifEnrich(
  ex_pfm, test_seq, rm_seq, min_score = score_thresh, model = "quasi", mc.cores = cores
)
iter_res <- testMotifEnrich(
  ex_pfm, test_seq, rm_seq, min_score = score_thresh, mc.cores = cores, model = "iteration"
)

workflows.name: clustered_motif_analysis
workflows.intent: Group highly similar motifs into clusters to reduce redundancy, and test the clusters for positional bias and enrichment.
workflows.stages: 1. Cluster similar motifs using clusterMotifs() ;; 2. Split the PFMs into clusters ;; 3. Find matches for clustered motifs using getClusterMatches() ;; 4. Test clustered motifs for positional bias using testClusterPos() ;; 5. Test clustered motifs for enrichment using testClusterEnrich()
workflows.code:
cl <- clusterMotifs(ex_pfm, plot = TRUE, labels = NULL)
ex_cl <- split(ex_pfm, cl)
names(ex_cl) <- vapply(split(names(cl), cl), paste, character(1), collapse = "/")
cl_matches <- getClusterMatches(
    ex_cl, test_seq, min_score = score_thresh, best_only = TRUE
)
testClusterPos(cl_matches, test_seq, abs = TRUE)
testClusterEnrich(
  ex_cl, test_seq, rm_seq, min_score = score_thresh, model = "quasi", mc.cores = cores
)
